title: Eight-to-four nights in New Orleans building strength
summary: New Orleans musicians played eight until four in the morning, which Turetsky says builds strength; players learned new numbers on the job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Was New Orleans the same thing?
8:00 o'clock till 4:00 o'clock in the morning.

You know, that's something I must ask you about this. I have a theory, let me see if my theory makes any sense to you -- when a man stands up and plays from 8:00 o'clock at night till 4:00 in the morning, you really develop strength, you know. Right, you really get your chops togethers, as it were, and that's where you really learn how to play.
Got a chance to practice (unintelligible) them all, got a new number there, come on let's play and that number --
-- (unintelligible) after all the tunes you playing, run back to that same number again, try to learn it. Cats had all kind of ways to get -- to get rid of something or learn this -- something.
